 Updated: 6:05 AM EST Nov 12, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Michelle Kennedy Meteorologist Dylan Hudler Meteorologist Brian Slocum Meteorologist By Michael Pardee WINSTON-SALEM, N.C. — After several seasonably warm North Carolina afternoons this week, a blast of colder Canadian air will bring down temperatures across much of the East Coast this weekend. A sudden stratospheric warming event has caused at least a temporary collapse of the Polar Vortex , allowing colder Arctic air to spill south from the Arctic Circle and reach as far as the Carolinas and Georgia.

This may also mean the season's first snowfall along the Blue Ridge Parkway and parts of the Shenandoah Valley in Virginia, especially on the western slopes. 
 Potential snowfall from Thursday, Nov. 12, through Saturday, Nov. 14
 Hearst Owned Snowfall totals appear light, ranging from a dusting to a few inches along west-facing slopes. The WXII 12 First Warning Weather Team will continue to monitor this potent storm and fine-tune the forecast as needed. 
 What to Expect in the Mountains
 Mountain residents can prepare for inclement weather beginning as early as Thursday, Nov. 12, and lingering through Saturday, Nov. 14.
 Reduced visibility from rain, blowing snow, and wintry mix is possible
 Driving difficulties from slick to slippery road conditions
 Bitter cold winds may make air temperatures feel like the teens and single digits
 Strong wind gusts may cause sporadic power outages
 What to Expect in the Piedmont Triad & Foothills 
 Residents in the Piedmont Triad and Foothills can prepare for the coldest air of the season so far. Freezing temperatures are likely by Sunday morning, Nov. 15.
 Scattered light rain is possible early Thursday morning
 Getting windy Thursday afternoon 
 Windy and colder weather Friday and Saturday 
 Temperatures may run about 10 to 15 degrees below normal, with lows in the low 30s and highs in the low 50s on Saturday and Sunday
